pack.title: A grant, a ford and a rising castle

presentation.anchor: Hugh de Lacy · Áth Troim · Trim Castle
presentation.question: How do paper, earth and stone show who gains power and who bears its cost?
presentation.opening: Later grant copies and the castle fabric make conquest administration visible without turning the story into empty-land progress.
presentation.evidenceLimit: Grant and castle show imposed authority; neither makes conquest consent or supports an invented foundation-day scene.
presentation.sourceTitle: Later grant copies and Trim Castle fabric
presentation.sourceDetail: Grant dated 1172 · building phases require specialist bounds
presentation.artifactPrompt: Keep ford, grant and building phases visibly distinct.
presentation.tegCanDo: Say what you have, locate familiar things and describe a place.

pages.title: A country written as a gift
pages.body: Henry II granted Meath to Hugh de Lacy; the text reaches us through later manuscript copies.

pages.title: Crossing becomes centre
pages.body: The ford and routes help explain Trim's choice as an administrative centre without pretending the place was empty.

pages.title: Timber, earth, stone
pages.body: An early fortification followed the grant; the large stone complex developed through later work.
pages.detail: No single foundation-day picture can carry the phases honestly.

pages.title: Hold place and power together
pages.body: Choose the explanation that uses geography without excusing conquest.

exercise.objective: Connect route and river to imposed authority without erasing existing people.
exercise.prompt: Why does the story begin at the ford?
exercise.answer: Route and river help explain why authority was fixed here.

options.text: The castle appeared before anyone used the place.
options.rationale: That erases the existing place and communities.

options.text: Route and river help explain why authority was fixed here.
options.rationale: Geography supports the choice without justifying the conquest.

options.text: The grant proves everyone welcomed the new lordship.
options.rationale: A royal grant cannot establish consent.

exercise.feedback: Place explains the choice without excusing the conquest.
exercise.hint: Use the ford to explain the location, not the legitimacy of the grant.
exercise.recovery: That version erases evidence or people the story must keep visible.

pages.title: A castle is also pressure
pages.body: Walls organise defence and administration, but they also materialise conquest and dispossession.
pages.detail: Specialist and sensitivity review remain open before this preview can expand.
